title: Decidability of stability under arbitrary switching
decision_reason: Explicit sourced question, independent scholarly corroboration, current theorem/version comparisons, duplicate audit and separated A44 adversarial self-review passed.
aliases: absolute asymptotic stability of rational discrete linear inclusions
strict subunit joint spectral radius decision problem

problem_fingerprint.objects: Positive integers n,m and a finite list A_1,...,A_m in Q^(n x n), given exactly by finite binary encodings of rational numerators and nonzero denominators.
problem_fingerprint.quantifiers: One algorithm must halt on every input, with n and m unbounded across inputs; its YES condition is convergence to zero for every real initial state and every infinite switching signal.
problem_fingerprint.observable: Convergence ||x_k||_2 -> 0 as k -> infinity; equivalently the joint spectral radius is strictly less than one.
problem_fingerprint.conclusion: Decide whether such a total algorithm exists. No polynomial-time requirement and no separation promise around the threshold.
problem_fingerprint.scope: Ordinary real linear dynamics with rationally specified modes; unrestricted switching. Not boundedness, the nonstrict threshold rho<=1, mortality, one chosen switching policy, Markov switching, or dwell-time constraints. Equivalent JSR formulation is one entry.

resolution_scope_comparisons.input_match: Finite rational matrices, including two-mode instances.
resolution_scope_comparisons.target_difference: Decides boundedness or rho<=1, not rho<1. Section 1 explicitly leaves the latter question unresolved.

resolution_scope_comparisons.extra_hypothesis: The family has the finiteness property.
resolution_scope_comparisons.target_difference: The enumeration argument's boundary termination uses that hypothesis; arbitrary rational inputs have no such promise.

resolution_scope_comparisons.input_match: Finite real matrix families, hence rational inputs are included.
resolution_scope_comparisons.conclusion: Existence of a contracting polynomial norm characterizes stable cases.
resolution_scope_comparisons.target_difference: No degree bound or total procedure with negative termination is supplied.
resolution_scope_comparisons.assessment: Complete positive certificate characterization, not a total decider.

resolution_scope_comparisons.input_match: Theorem 8 discusses ordinary positive matrices; Theorems 1 and 7 discuss bilinear maps.
resolution_scope_comparisons.target_difference: Undecidability statements retain <=1; computability is approximation. Strict positivity of entries is not strictness of the threshold.
resolution_scope_comparisons.assessment: No transfer to the requested strict rational-matrix decision problem.

resolution_scope_comparisons.source: MR26, accessible author-version Theorems 2.5–2.7 and Algorithm 3.1
resolution_scope_comparisons.extra_hypothesis: Certificate tree/vertices or spectrum-maximizing candidate products; termination is conditional.
resolution_scope_comparisons.target_difference: Wider applicability of the certificate algorithm does not establish a finite answer for every rational input.
resolution_scope_comparisons.assessment: Reviewed author-version scope does not settle the question; journal full-text access limit retained.

resolution_scope_comparisons.source: NJ26 v2, Theorem 4; Algorithm 1 and Remark 2
resolution_scope_comparisons.input_match: Finite ordinary matrix families under arbitrary switching.
resolution_scope_comparisons.extra_hypothesis: Attained graph optimization optimum and tight subgraph with at most one outgoing edge per node.
resolution_scope_comparisons.target_difference: The theorem proves exactness under these conditions. Remark 2 explicitly provides no termination or convergence guarantee.
resolution_scope_comparisons.assessment: Current September 10 version does not give a total decider.

resolution_scope_comparisons.target_difference: Non-semialgebraicity rules out a finite polynomial description over real parameters, not an arbitrary Turing algorithm on rational inputs.
resolution_scope_comparisons.assessment: Distinct computational barrier, not an undecidability proof for this target.
